origin.description: Gini coefficient of a numeric vector.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Numeric vector. The measures are defined for non-negative values.

arguments.name: corr
arguments.text: If true, apply the finite-sample correction: divide by n - 1 instead of n.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If true, drop missing values first. If false, any missing value makes the result missing.

origin.details: Values are sorted and weighted by ranks 1 through n. The coefficient is 2 * sum(x * rank) / sum(x) - (n + 1), divided by n. corr=TRUE divides by n - 1 instead. ineq() calls Gini without that correction.
origin.value: A single number, the Gini coefficient.
origin.example:
# generate vector (of incomes)
x <- c(541, 1463, 2445, 3438, 4437, 5401, 6392, 8304, 11904, 22261)
# compute Gini coefficient
ineq(x)

translation.description: Gini coefficient of a numeric vector.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Numeric vector. The measures are defined for non-negative values. Missing values are NaN.

arguments.name: corr
arguments.text: If true, apply the finite-sample correction: divide by n - 1 instead of n.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If true, drop missing values first. If false, any missing value makes the result NaN.

translation.details: Values are sorted and weighted by ranks 1 through n. The coefficient is 2 * sum(x * rank) / sum(x) - (n + 1), divided by n. corr=True divides by n - 1 instead. ineq() calls Gini without that correction.
translation.value: A single number, the Gini coefficient.
translation.example:
from ineq.measures import ineq

# generate vector (of incomes)
x = [541, 1463, 2445, 3438, 4437, 5401, 6392, 8304, 11904, 22261]
# compute Gini coefficient
print(ineq(x))
